274259.deck: A martial-arts champion fights an alien invasion.

overview.text: Winning a television competition is only the start of Wild Dog’s trouble. He has to defend the planet in a 3D brawler, gaining new abilities as he defeats enemies.

development.text: Com2uS developed and published the Zeebo edition.

280386.deck: Alice solves puzzles with four companions and a second Wonderland behind the mirrors.

overview.text: Alice can cross between Wonderland and its mirror world. The White Rabbit alters time, the Cheshire Cat reveals hidden objects, the March Hare moves them, and the Mad Hatter sends them between worlds. Reaching the next area means working out whose ability to use and where.

development.text: Disney Interactive Studios Beijing developed the film tie-in. Zeebo Interactive Studios handled the console adaptation, led by Danny Caldas with producer Hugo Faria. The credits also name Olímpio MacLouly and Thomas Gomes as developers, and Denis Koishi as musician.

release.text: Alice was part of the Disney Mobile lineup announced for Zeebo in September 2010. The game also appeared under the English title Alice in Wonderland: An Adventure Beyond the Mirror.

276151.deck: Ski and snowboard down mountain courses, with jumps along the way.

overview.text: Alpine Racer offers downhill skiing and snowboarding. Players choose a character, race through snowy courses and perform aerial tricks.

development.text: This Alpine Racer came from Namco’s mobile lineup. Its BREW edition appeared in 2008, followed by iPhone and Zeebo versions in 2009. Namco Bandai Games is credited as developer, with Namco Networks publishing and Tectoy distributing the Zeebo release.

280214.deck: Propeller aircraft fight over a fictional Second World War.

overview.text: Armageddon Squadron is an arcade flight game. Its missions send the player against air and ground targets in a fictional Second World War setting.

development.text: Polarbit developed the game and announced a Zeebo version in April 2010.

release.text: The Zeebo release reached Brazil in September 2010, distributed by Zeebo Brasil.

277083.deck: Rotate four gems at a time to build matches.

overview.text: Bejeweled Twist changes the usual gem swap into a rotation. Turning a group of coloured stones lines up matches and can set off further combinations.

development.text: The Zeebo credits distinguish the original design by Brian Fiete, Jason Kapalka and Kurt Pfeifer from the later engineering and production teams. Vincent McCreith is credited for music on this edition.

release.text: By March 2010, Bejeweled Twist was already available on Zeebo in Brazil and Mexico.

274214.deck: Crash and his rivals race karts and attack each other with collected items.

overview.text: Crash Bandicoot Nitro Kart 3D puts the series’ characters into item-filled kart races. The Zeebo guide advertises courses that run from underwater environments to space.

development.text: Polarbit made the original mobile game using its Fuse technology. Tectoy Digital adapted it for Zeebo. Tiago Tex Pine and Hugo Faria handled production; the programming credits name Vitor Picanço do Amaral, Tiago Monteiro Fernandes, Leonardo Loures Lopes and Bruno Evangelista.

280173.deck: Six card games with Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Daisy and Goofy.

overview.text: Disney All Star Cards brings together six card games. Each table has one human player and three computer opponents. Pixie dust can buy cards and gallery artwork, or be spent on a game-specific cheat.

release.text: Disney Mobile announced the Zeebo edition on 1 September 2010, with a target launch date of 21 September.

274754.deck: Billy and Jimmy Lee return in a six-mission remake.

overview.text: Billy and Jimmy Lee set out to rescue Marian from Machine Gun Willy’s gang. The Zeebo remake expands the arcade game from four missions to six, with three new locations. Weapons dropped by enemies can be picked up and used, and oil drums can be thrown or kicked.
Finishing the game opens up more playable fighters. The extra battle mode lets players return as the enemies, with eighteen unlockable characters and their own sets of moves.

development.text: Brizo Interactive and Million are credited on this remake. Its Zeebo staff include main planner Hiroto Ikuta, main programmer Seiji Ando, graphic artists Hiroto Kittaka and Yuji Watanabe, and composer Hideki Asanaka. Souta Ichino led the project, with Ryosuke Jinno as sub-producer.
Brizo later made an iPhone Double Dragon. In an April 2011 interview, Jinno described that release as the studio’s third Double Dragon project, following its earlier mobile and Zeebo work.

274803.deck: Football with friendly matches, challenges, seasons and tournaments.

overview.text: FIFA 09 on Zeebo offers four modes: a friendly match for one or two players, ten set challenges, a full season in one of eleven leagues, and a choice of ten tournaments. Players can change their lineup and roles, while a stamina meter limits continuous running.

development.text: Gamelion developed this edition for Electronic Arts. Its credits name Krzysztof Jędruczyk as development lead and Hubert Borowy and Sebastian Szczygieł as producers. Wojciech Lekki handled 3D art.

277380.deck: A Terran mercenary takes contracts in the war against the Vossk.

overview.text: Galaxy on Fire puts the player in a spacecraft as a Terran mercenary fighting the Vossk.

development.text: Fishlabs adapted Galaxy on Fire using its ABYSS engine. Michael Schade explained which versions supplied the code and artwork:
The first Zeebo builds ran too slowly. The team reduced assets and reorganised textures, eventually reaching roughly four times its initial frame rate.
Television output introduced other constraints. Strong colours could bleed and fine horizontal lines could flicker; the absence of OpenAL required changes to the sound engine.

278200.deck: Drive a tank through waves of aircraft, vehicles and heavier weapons.

overview.text: Heavy Weapon is a side-scrolling tank shooter with enemies attacking from land, sea and air. Equipment upgrades are available between stages.

development.text: Vega Mobile made the Zeebo version from an existing mobile adaptation. The credits name Wayne Imlach, René Laurent, Eric Thommerot and Philip Plunkett on that earlier work, with Viktorya Hollings as executive producer of the Zeebo edition.

release.text: Heavy Weapon had launched in Brazil and Mexico by PopCap’s March 2010 Zeebo announcement.

studio_roles.name: Vega Mobile
studio_roles.role: Zeebo adaptation based on mobile version

280221.deck: Turn-based robot battles between the Corporation and the Rebellion.

overview.text: Iron Sight gives each side time to move and aim before firing. Players fight for the Corporation or the Rebellion, using missiles and items such as teleporters. Holding the fire button increases a shot’s range; releasing it launches the weapon.

development.text: The Zeebo credits name Deion Mobile as the developer and list five authors: Tomek Wagner, Raymond Leung, Bartek Tajer, Vyach Imalkovski and Justin Wasack.

release.text: Polarbit brought Iron Sight to Zeebo. It was available in Brazil and Mexico by the end of September 2010.

276121.deck: Build a racing crew and take on rival teams across the city.

overview.text: The crew house is the hub for choosing cars, checking the city map and managing teammates. Events include taking down rival cars and escaping an enemy crew’s territory before time runs out.

development.text: Tectoy Digital made the Zeebo version of Own the City, sold here as Domine a Cidade. Hugo Faria produced it, Bruno Evangelista led programming and Seigi Sato led art. The larger adaptation team included programmers Gustavo Galembeck and Tiago Monteiro Fernandes, with music by Denis Koishi.

278962.deck: Fire a ball into the board and clear every orange peg.

overview.text: Peggle turns each shot into a bouncing path through a field of pegs. Its ten masters supply different powers for clearing the orange targets.

release.text: Peggle was available on Zeebo by 9 March 2010. PopCap’s announcement lists 55 main levels, ten unlockable masters, Quick Play, Duel, and a further 55 Challenge levels.

280238.deck: Race powerboats around buoys and unlock new islands.

overview.text: Powerboat Challenge offers four pilots with boats that have different handling traits. A tutorial explains steering and passing the buoys. Completing enough events opens the next island, with conventional races and elimination events among the challenges.

development.text: Fishlabs developed the game. The Zeebo credits name Lars Berger and Stefan Görlich as lead developers, Henning Lubahn for 3D and level design, and Gero Goerlich for music and sound effects. Jörg Thomaschewski produced it.

276154.deck: The mobile Prey adaptation, brought to Zeebo as Prey Evil.

overview.text: Prey Evil belongs to the mobile branch of Prey. Machineworks Northwest developed it using QSound’s Ripp3D renderer.

development.text: The Zeebo credits name Seth A. Robinson as lead programmer, Andreas Vasen as producer and Scott Miller as executive producer. Les Pardew and Weston Tracy are credited for art.

release.text: In June 2009, QSound said Zeebo purchasers were entitled to download Prey Evil free of charge.

274802.deck: Fight through military bases, castles and dungeons filled with monsters.

overview.text: Quake sends the player through military bases, medieval castles and lava-filled dungeons in search of four runes. Knights, ogres and other creatures stand in the way. Finding keys and hidden supplies is as much a part of reaching the exit as surviving the next fight.

development.text: The Zeebo adaptation retains credits for the original id Software team alongside a separate console production and programming group.

Rafael Nanya and Heriberto Martinez Manrique are credited as the Zeebo chief engineers. The port’s programmers include Cesar Dantas de Castro, Ricardo Destro, Rafael Dazcal, Ademir José Barba and Mauricio Antonio Guerta. André Penha and Reinaldo Normand served as executive producers.

release.text: Quake and Quake II were removed from ZeeboNet in June 2010. The free-download offer switched to Zeebo Extreme Rolimã and Jetboard.

276153.deck: A surviving soldier takes the fight to the Strogg homeworld.

overview.text: After the Strogg attack Earth, humanity launches an assault on their homeworld. The operation fails, leaving a surviving soldier to fight through the aliens’ military installations and disable their war machine. Quake II builds its first-person shooting around this campaign through enemy territory.

development.text: Tectoy Digital ported and localised Quake II for Zeebo. Its team appears in a separate section alongside the original id Software credits.

Tiago Tex Pine produced the adaptation. Its programmers include Edgar Vilela Gadbem, Gustavo Galembeck, Vitor Picanço do Amaral and Henrique Mendes. Denis Koishi handled sound. The Portuguese voices include Suzana Bueno as the computers and Bruno Santos on the radio; members of the programming team voiced prisoners.

release.text: The Brazilian Zeebo edition dates to 2009. It was removed from ZeeboNet with Quake in June 2010.

280602.deck: An arcade street racer from Polarbit’s Zeebo lineup.

overview.text: Raging Thunder 2 is an arcade street-racing game. Polarbit announced it for Zeebo alongside Armageddon Squadron, Iron Sight and Deliverace.

development.text: Pixelbite includes Raging Thunder 2 in its own game portfolio. GameFAQs credits Pixelbite as developer of the Zeebo edition and Polarbit as publisher; Polarbit’s contemporary announcement confirms the console release.

release.text: The Zeebo version arrived in December 2010.

studio_roles.name: Pixelbite
studio_roles.role: Developer credited by GameFAQs; title appears in studio portfolio

278282.deck: Rally stages on asphalt, loose stones, sand and snow.

overview.text: Rally Master Pro offers four modes across courses with different surfaces. The Zeebo guide lists asphalt, stones, sand and snow.

development.text: Fishlabs developed and published the game. It began on Java phones in 2008, then reached Zeebo in Brazil in December 2009, with Tectoy handling distribution.

overview.text: Reckless Racing follows cars around off-road tracks from an overhead viewpoint. Pixelbite developed the game.

release.text: The game appeared in Zeebo’s announced Polarbit lineup under its earlier name, Deliverace. The Zeebo edition followed in 2010.

276675.deck: Leon’s rescue mission retold in twelve chapters for the mobile and Zeebo editions.

overview.text: Resident Evil 4 Zeebo Edition breaks Leon’s rescue mission into twelve chapters, joined by cutscenes. It keeps the over-the-shoulder view and requires him to stop moving before he fires. The Merchant sells weapons and items using money earned during play.

development.text: The Zeebo release credits Ideaworks3D as developer, Capcom as publisher and Tectoy as distributor. HI Corporation separately confirmed that this version used its MascotCapsule eruption technology.

release.text: The Zeebo edition was released in Brazil in August 2009.

276152.deck: Namco’s mobile Ridge Racer, adapted for a television and controller.

overview.text: Ridge Racer offers car selection and three-dimensional road racing through city, mountain and coastal settings.

development.text: The Zeebo game comes from the redesigned mobile edition of Ridge Racer. That version is catalogued separately from the original arcade and PlayStation games.

277455.deck: Regret searches for his past in an action RPG.

overview.text: Zenonia follows Regret through an adventure built around exploration, equipment and choices that affect his journey.

development.text: GAMEVIL brought its mobile action RPG to Zeebo. The company announced the console release in November 2009.

279712.deck: Fire coloured balls into moving chains and fight the island’s tiki bosses.

overview.text: Zuma’s Revenge returns to the ball-shooting puzzle game with hostile spirits and tiki bosses. Matching colours clears sections of the advancing chains.

development.text: Vega Mobile ported PopCap’s game to Zeebo. Reflective Audio is credited for music.

release.text: The Brazilian Zeebo release followed in July 2010.

274804.deck: Twenty brain-training activities with daily progress tracking.

overview.text: Treino Cerebral is the Portuguese title of Gameloft’s Brain Challenge. Its 20 activities are divided into five categories, with daily exercises and charts that track the player’s results.

development.text: Gameloft’s Zeebo team was led by producer Alan Olvera and lead programmers Carlos Zarate and Favio Medrano. Enrique Nevarez handled 2D art, while Henri-Pierre Pellegrin worked on sound and music.

release.text: Treino Cerebral was one of three Portuguese-language games installed on the first Brazilian retail consoles when sales began on 25 May 2009.

studio_roles.name: Gameloft
studio_roles.role: Developer of Brain Challenge / Treino Cerebral

280634.deck: Six learning activities with Mônica, Magali, Cascão and their friends.

overview.text: Vamos Brincar nº 1 combines counting, colours, jigsaws, memory games and mazes. Anjinho needs particular balloons popped; Magali wants matching fruit found; Mônica helps Cascão cross a river and searches for Sansão. Marina’s painting activity also includes a free drawing tool.
There are three difficulty levels and 30 achievements. Players can import a Zeeboid to keep track of their achievements.

development.text: The game was made by Zeebo Interactive Studios in Campinas with Mauricio de Sousa Productions. Their November 2010 licensing announcement proposed nine educational and entertainment titles, including activity centres and games about maths and language.
Artist Alexandre Nacari identifies animation, assets and the graphical interface as his contributions. His portfolio names Flash and Photoshop as the tools he used for this 2010 project.

release.text: The Brazilian Zeebo game was released on 21 December 2010. Its published title is also recorded as Turma da Mônica em Vamos Brincar nº 1; this archive retains OpenZeebo’s “Vol. 1” label.

studio_roles.name: Mauricio de Sousa Productions
studio_roles.role: Licensed characters; animation and Portuguese voices

279036.deck: Toto and Willy’s platform adventure from the Mexican film Una Película de Huevos.

overview.text: Toto wants to become a chicken. Confi retells that journey in an alternative story based on Una Película de Huevos, with Toto and Willy as playable characters and a third character to unlock.
The game has 25 stages, five boss fights and ten unlockable competition stages. Two players can cooperate or race each other.

development.text: Fabrication Games developed the game, with Tommy Palm directing and Alexander Ekvall leading development and game design. David Telenius designed the levels, Henrik Pettersson led the art, and Oskar Rahm worked on 3D art and animation.
Huevocartoon’s team supplied the film characters and cutscenes. Jarpa Studio is credited for sound production.

release.text: Un Juego de Huevos launched in Mexico on 19 April 2010. Brazil received it as Um Jogo de Ovos on 24 August 2010.

studio_roles.name: Comunidad Huevo, S.A. de C.V. / Huevocartoon

274755.deck: The console’s main menu and game launcher.

overview.text: Z-Wheel starts when the console boots. It is the interface owners used to browse and open the games they had acquired.

development.text: O3 Labs documents several Brazilian software versions, including 1.0.368 and 1.0.727, alongside a Mexican 1.0.696.5 build.

274791.deck: A small system application recorded separately from Z-Wheel.

overview.text: Zeebo App appears as a separate entry in the console’s software inventory under ID 274791. Z-Wheel, which supplies the main menu and game launcher, has its own entry under ID 274755.

notes.text: The application’s exact user function and development credits have not been established for this record.

277495.deck: Web pages and curated channels on a television.

overview.text: The Portuguese game guide calls this service Z-Channels. It let owners browse the web through their television; OpenZeebo identifies the preserved application as Zeebo Channels (Opera Mini).

development.text: Opera Software adapted Opera Mini for Zeebo. The browser compressed web content before delivery over the mobile connection, while the console displayed pages on the television.

release.text: Opera and Zeebo announced Opera Mini for Mexico on 1 December 2009.

In Brazil, a 10 September 2010 official post said Z-Channels was already available. The application download was free; browsing time was sold in two-, four- or six-hour packages using Z-Credits, with two hours included on the first download.

studio_roles.name: Opera Software
studio_roles.scope: Opera Mini for Zeebo — Mexico announcement, 2009

279394.deck: Zeebo news, release announcements and promotions on the console.

overview.text: Zeebo Clube was a free application for following news from Zeebo without leaving the console. The company described release announcements, promotions and other information about the system.

release.text: Zeebo Brasil introduced the application on its official blog on 3 September 2010 and directed owners to install it from the console’s store. The post said availability for everyone would follow.

notes.text: The official post distinguished Zeebo Clube from ZeeboClub, an independent fan website with a similar name.

277727.deck: Off-road buggy racing with jumps and turbo boosts.

overview.text: Baja races small off-road cars across dirt tracks, caves and rough ground. Jumps interrupt the course, and collected fuel supplies a turbo boost.

development.text: Tiago Tex Pine led game design and production across the five Extreme games. He described the work involved:
The team grew to 23 while making the series during 2009, working towards a schedule of one finished game every two months.

release.text: Tectoy released Baja for Zeebo on 31 October 2009.

quotes.text: my team had to create a console-looking 3D racing game from scratch without any pre-built engine
quotes.speaker: Tiago Tex Pine
quotes.attribution: Producer and designer; portfolio account updated 5 October 2025.

studio_roles.name: Tectoy Digital
studio_roles.original_name: Tectoy Digital / Tec Toy Desenvolvimento Digital Ltda.

overview.text: Bóia Cross sends its riders down rapids in inner tubes. Energy drinks replenish the boost, and the guide advertises special tricks. Its three courses are named Santo André, Bonito and Caverna do Diabo.

development.text: Tiago Tex Pine led design across the Extreme series. Level layouts were worked out with the 3D environment artists and QA staff.

release.text: Bóia Cross was released for Zeebo on 21 December 2009. It is also known as Zeebo Extreme Acqua Ride.

studio_roles.name: Tectoy Digital
studio_roles.original_name: Tectoy Digital / Tec Toy Desenvolvimento Digital Ltda.

277285.deck: Aeroplane races through canyons, caves and tunnels.

overview.text: Corrida Aérea has three circuits raced over three laps. Flying through rings refills the aircraft’s turbo. The Portuguese guide places its canyons, caves, bridges and tunnels in Chapada Diamantina.

development.text: The Extreme games and their tools were written in C++ using BREW APIs. The artists used additional 3ds Max scripts to export their work into the engine.

release.text: Corrida Aérea was released for Zeebo on 29 September 2009.

studio_roles.name: Tectoy Digital
studio_roles.original_name: Tectoy Digital / Tec Toy Desenvolvimento Digital Ltda.

278283.deck: Wakeboard racing with jetpacks, slalom gates and aerial tricks.

overview.text: Jetboard’s riders cross the water on wakeboards propelled by jetpacks. Passing obstacles on the indicated side and performing tricks refill the turbo. Missing five obstacles ends the race.
Its courses take their names from Angra dos Reis, Vitória and Fernando de Noronha. The guide highlights jumps, flips and avoiding obstacles.

development.text: Jetboard shares the Extreme series’ Boomerang motion-control support. Its art credits also name Animar Estúdio for additional work.

release.text: Jetboard was released for Zeebo on 21 December 2009.

studio_roles.name: Tectoy Digital
studio_roles.original_name: Tectoy Digital / Tec Toy Desenvolvimento Digital Ltda.

276809.deck: Downhill racing in a carrinho de rolimã.

overview.text: A carrinho de rolimã is a small soapbox cart. This racer sends four selectable characters down courses named after São Paulo, Petrópolis and Ouro Preto. Gravity carries the carts downhill; players brake, drift and use turbo.

development.text: Rolimã opened the five-game Extreme series. Tiago Tex Pine led its game and interface design, alongside production of the series.

release.text: Rolimã was released for Zeebo on 15 August 2009.

studio_roles.name: Tectoy Digital
studio_roles.original_name: Tectoy Digital / Tec Toy Desenvolvimento Digital Ltda.

279380.deck: Four football challenges starring the player’s Zeeboid.

overview.text: Foot Camp separates football into penalties, free kicks, dribbling and keep-ups. The free-kick game adds wind and a defensive wall; dribbling asks players to repeat button sequences. Power-ups can turn a goalkeeper into a chicken or have aliens abduct opponents.

development.text: Tiago Tex Pine designed Foot Camp for friends playing together. Three activities use turns and score comparisons, while Goal Scoring allows direct, simultaneous competition. He led a twelve-person team and worked on the game design, interface wireframes, balancing and user testing.
The game used C++, BREW and Adreno SDKs, with an internal OpenGL ES engine developed by Tectoy Digital and Zeebo Studios.

release.text: Zeebo announced Foot Camp and Zeeboids together on 3 June 2010 for Brazil and Mexico. Zeebo Interactive Studios in Brazil created both. The announcement described groups of up to eight taking turns.

quotes.text: everything in the game is inherently built for couch-multiplayer
quotes.speaker: Tiago Tex Pine
quotes.attribution: Producer and designer; portfolio account updated 5 October 2025.

280647.deck: Football with superpowers, custom teams and a career mode.

overview.text: Super League turns football into an arcade game with superpowers. Players create a team and take it through a career, using their Zeeboids as footballers.

development.text: Tiago Tex Pine led a team of fifteen and designed systems and power-ups. He describes the game as the result of three years working with Zeebo, during which the team revised its custom engine and built tools to get more from the Adreno graphics hardware.
Art direction was handled by Marcelo Marcati, with concept art by Rafael Marquetto and Wilson Hideki Akamine. Élcio Faria Ribeiro wrote the script and also worked in QA.

release.text: Super League was released on 22 December 2010 as Zeebo’s main Christmas title that year. Its Portuguese title is Zeebo F.C. Super Liga.

quotes.text: I consider Super League to be the best we could have done with the resources and knowledge we had.
quotes.speaker: Tiago Tex Pine
quotes.attribution: Producer and designer, reflecting on the project in his portfolio; updated 5 October 2025.

277229.deck: Seven minigames for one or two players.

overview.text: Family Pack lets players choose a character and compete in seven games: 8ball, Cannonball, Dirtbike, Formula 0.01, Long John Silver, Score and Zap. The Zeebo version supports one or two players.

development.text: Jadestone’s credited team had six people. Tommy Palm produced the collection, Alexander Ekvall led development, Henrik Pettersson was lead illustrator and Lina Hansson directed the art. Patrik Lindegren and Erik Olsson are the other developers named.

release.text: Family Pack arrived on Zeebo on 29 September 2009. Its seven games were subsequently released individually for mobile devices.

279159.deck: Peteca matches played with the hand instead of a racket.

overview.text: Peteca uses a shuttlecock struck with the hand. In the Boomerang version, the character moves around the court automatically and the player swings the controller to return it. The guide advertises unlockable outfits and courts.

development.text: Hugo Faria produced Peteca, with Bruno Evangelista leading programming. Its artists included Bruno Carias Fogaça, Paula Carneiro Amin, Suellen Carollo, Luiz Gustavo Marquetti and Seigi Sato.

release.text: Peteca first appeared as Boomerang Sports Peteca in May 2010. On 17 August, Zeebo announced its relaunch as Zeebo Sports Peteca with Z-Pad support.

studio_roles.original_name: Tectoy Digital / Tec Toy Desenvolvimento Digital Ltda.

278738.deck: Four-a-side dodgeball with the Zeebo Sports cast.

overview.text: Queimada is dodgeball. Its teams have four players, and the Boomerang version uses swinging motions to throw or dodge while characters move automatically. Buttons handle passing, catching and taunting.
The Portuguese guide also advertises new character outfits to unlock.

development.text: Hugo Faria produced the game. Bruno Evangelista and Tiago Monteiro Fernandes led programming, Seigi Sato led art, and Denis Koishi supplied music.

release.text: The original Boomerang Sports Queimada was released on 5 February 2010. Its Zeebo Sports relaunch added Z-Pad controls in August 2010; two-player games required matching controller types.

277534.deck: Doubles tennis with unlockable rackets and motion controls.

overview.text: Tênis plays doubles matches with characters that move automatically. With the Boomerang, the player swings to hit the ball. Winning earns points towards unusual rackets, including a guitar, broom and frying pan.

development.text: Bruno Evangelista led programming and Seigi Sato led art. The credits name Hugo Faria as producer and André Nogueira as acting producer, with further programming, art and testing recorded in a separate 2010 additional-resources section.

release.text: Tênis began as a Boomerang-only game on 15 October 2009. The August 2010 Zeebo Sports edition added Z-Pad play. Existing owners could request a free upgrade, which erased their local progress.

overview.text: Vôlei covers serving, attacks, blocks and defensive returns. Characters move automatically, while the player times actions with the controller. One or two players choose doubles teams, and victories earn points towards costumes.

development.text: Hugo Faria produced Vôlei. Bruno Evangelista and Tiago Monteiro Fernandes led programming; Seigi Sato led art, with Paula Carneiro Amin, Pedro Hamaya and Carina Cheng among the artists.

release.text: Vôlei was released on 14 December 2009 as Boomerang Sports Vôlei. The August 2010 Zeebo Sports relaunch added Z-Pad controls while keeping the same game.

studio_roles.name: Tectoy Digital
studio_roles.original_name: Tectoy Digital / Tec Toy Desenvolvimento Digital Ltda.

279382.deck: Create avatars for Foot Camp, Super League and other compatible games.

overview.text: Zeeboids creates 3D characters with customizable appearances. Compatible games use those characters as players, including Foot Camp and Super League.
At launch, players could synchronize their Zeeboids, skills and achievements through ZeeboNet and retrieve them on another console, such as a friend’s system.

development.text: Tiago Tex Pine led an eight-person team and handled the core product design. Nintendo’s Miis were an explicit inspiration. He worked with programmers to decide how much appearance customization the hardware could support while maintaining the frame rate.
The application used the team’s internal OpenGL ES engine with C++, BREW and Adreno SDKs.

release.text: Zeebo announced Zeeboids alongside Foot Camp in June 2010. Both were developed by Zeebo Interactive Studios in Brazil.

credits.name: Tiago Tex Pine
credits.role: Core product design; production and project management

279369.deck: Bounce a ball through alien formations and collect paddle upgrades.

overview.text: Alien Breaker Deluxe uses a paddle and ball to clear formations of alien blocks. Some blocks take several hits; others release bonuses that change the paddle, add weapons or protect the bottom of the screen.
Arcade and Challenge cover 100 levels across ten zones. Versus gives each player a separate playfield, while Fronton has two players competing on the same screen.

development.text: Vega Mobile expanded its earlier iPhone game for Zeebo, adding a new storyline and doubling the number of levels.

release.text: The Zeebo edition was released on 20 May 2010.

279888.deck: Blade and Striker fight the ninjas who kidnapped the president.

overview.text: Blade and Striker are recruited to rescue President Ronnie from the DragonNinja clan. Bad Dudes is a side-scrolling brawler: the two street fighters punch and kick their way through the kidnappers.

development.text: Data East created the original game. Onan Games handled the Zeebo port, published by G-Mode.

release.text: The Brazilian Zeebo release is dated 27 July 2010, alongside Heavy Barrel.

278986.deck: Joe and Mac take clubs and thrown weapons into dinosaur country.

overview.text: Joe and Mac fight dinosaurs and members of a rival tribe in a prehistoric platform game. They can attack up close or throw weapons at enemies beyond their clubs’ reach.

development.text: Onan Games adapted Data East’s game for Zeebo. G-Mode announced Caveman Ninja with Spinmaster and Street Slam in March 2010.

release.text: Release records date the Mexican edition to 31 March 2010 and the Brazilian edition to 16 April.

279233.deck: Choose a knight, bard, magician or ninja for a fantasy dungeon adventure.

overview.text: Dark Seal offers four heroes with different weapons: a knight, bard, magician and ninja. Alongside their ordinary attacks, spells and transformations give them other ways to fight through the monsters.

development.text: The Zeebo port was made by Onan Games from Data East’s original. G-Mode published it.

release.text: The Brazilian Zeebo release is dated 4 May 2010. International records also list the game as Gate of Doom.

279889.deck: Infiltrate a missile base and assemble a weapon from six hidden parts.

overview.text: Heavy Barrel is an overhead shooter set in a nuclear missile installation seized by terrorists. Its most powerful weapon was dismantled and locked away: the player collects keys and recovers its six parts while fighting through the base. Two players can tackle the mission together.

development.text: The original Data East arcade game appeared in 1987. Its credits name Koji Akibayashi for game design and Azusa Hara and Hiroaki Yoshida for music and sound. Onan Games later handled the Zeebo port.

release.text: Heavy Barrel reached the Brazilian Zeebo catalog on 27 July 2010, published by G-Mode.

279126.deck: A one-on-one fighter also released as Fighter’s History Dynamite.

overview.text: Karnov’s Revenge is a one-on-one fighting game. Pick a fighter and combine normal attacks and special moves to defeat the rest of the roster.

development.text: Onan Games made the Zeebo port of Data East’s fighter. It was part of G-Mode’s announced 2010 Data East lineup.

release.text: Listed internationally as Fighter’s History Dynamite, it arrived in Mexico on 13 April 2010 and Brazil on 16 April.

279200.deck: Match colored balls before the descending pile fills the playfield.

overview.text: Magical Drop III is a fast matching puzzle game built around colored balls. The Zeebo guide lists Survival, Challenge and Magical Journey as its three modes.

development.text: Onan Games handled the Zeebo port of Data East’s puzzle game. G-Mode included it in its March 2010 announcement.

release.text: The Brazilian Zeebo release is dated 22 April 2010.

276212.deck: Collect dots in isometric mazes while avoiding the ghosts.

overview.text: Pac-Mania moves PAC-MAN’s dot collecting into an isometric maze. Clear the dots to reach the next round, use power pellets to turn the tables on the ghosts, and jump over pursuers when the route is blocked. Some ghosts can jump too.

development.text: Namco released the arcade original in 1987. Tomoyuki Shimizu designed the game, with Shimizu and Toru Iwatani credited as directors. The Zeebo release record names Namco Bandai Games as the port developer and publisher.

release.text: Pac-Mania was released for Zeebo in Brazil on 16 June 2009, distributed by Tectoy.

278987.deck: Johnny and Tom pursue a kidnapped girlfriend with a magical yo-yo.

overview.text: Johnny and Tom set off on a treasure hunt after a kidnapping. Their weapons include a magical yo-yo, used to fight through the platform stages.

development.text: Spin Master was among the first three Data East games announced for Zeebo in March 2010. Onan Games made the port for publisher G-Mode.

release.text: Release records list Spinmaster in Mexico on 31 March 2010 and Brazil on 16 April.

278988.deck: Three-a-side basketball with high jumps and exaggerated dunks.

overview.text: Street Hoop plays basketball with three-player teams. Matches emphasize quick attacks, high jumps and exaggerated slam dunks.

development.text: G-Mode’s March 2010 announcement used the name Street Slam. Onan Games ported the Data East game to Zeebo.

release.text: The Brazilian Zeebo edition is dated 16 April 2010. The game also appears in international catalogs as Street Slam and Dunk Dream.

279125.deck: Jump on burger ingredients to drop them onto the plates below.

overview.text: Peter Pepper Jr. and his twin brother Pete assemble burgers by jumping on their ingredients. Each layer drops toward a serving plate, with food enemies chasing the cooks around the platforms and ladders. Falling ingredients can crush those enemies.

development.text: Data East released the arcade original in 1990. Its credits name Koji Akibayashi as game designer, Mario Watanabe and Yoshiyuki Urushibara as graphic designers, and Tatsuya Kiuchi and Tomoyoshi Sato for sound. Onan Games made the Zeebo port.

release.text: G-Mode announced Super Burger Time for Zeebo in March 2010. The Brazilian release is dated 16 April.

276731.deck: Namco’s second Iron Fist Tournament, released for Zeebo in 2009.

overview.text: Tekken 2 is a one-on-one fighting game. The Zeebo guide advertises 25 fighters and move sets from the arcade game.

development.text: Seiichi Ishii directed and designed the original Namco arcade game. Its credits also name Masahiro Kimoto as motion manager.

release.text: Namco Bandai Games America published Tekken 2 for Zeebo in Brazil on 8 October 2009, with Tectoy handling distribution.

280463.deck: Two cavemen clear creature-filled platform stages with clubs, fire and ice.

overview.text: A scientist named Ragor travels into the past and kidnaps Kama. Tork and Kral pursue him through 60 levels, fighting dinosaurs, bears and other creatures with clubs. Fire and ice upgrades let the cavemen trap enemies before finishing them off.
The game supports two players working together. Its Escape mode changes the objective to climbing fast enough to stay ahead of the scrolling screen.

development.text: Vega Mobile developed Tork and Kral under the earlier name Ice and Rock. In a 24 September 2010 report based on contact with the studio, ZeeboBrasil named Jerome Schurch as producer and reported that the game was awaiting Zeebo’s approval.

release.text: Vega Mobile released the game for Zeebo on 16 November 2010.

overview.text: Toy Raid puts the player behind a cannon, defending a base from toy aircraft and parachuting soldiers. Bombs threaten the base from above; soldiers who land can attack it from inside. Power-ups add guided bullets, scatter shots and other weapons.

263019.deck: Chess with animated mechanical pieces and 3D capture sequences.

overview.text: Ultimate Chess 3D plays on a conventional chessboard, then switches to animated battles when a piece captures another. Its mechanical pieces can be customized with parts bought through the game’s foundry.

development.text: Superscape’s game appeared on BREW phones in 2007 before reaching Zeebo in 2009. The Zeebo credit transcription names Viacheslav Dubikovsky as producer, Brian Collins as game designer and Ian Livingstone for sound and music.

release.text: Glu Mobile published the Zeebo edition in 2009.

279173.deck: Five heroes fight monsters with weapons and magic.

overview.text: Wizard Fire offers five fantasy heroes with different attacks. The adventure combines weapon combat, magic and treasure collecting.

development.text: Onan Games ported Data East’s game to Zeebo. G-Mode announced it in March 2010 under the spelling Wizard of Fire.

release.text: Wizard Fire was released for Zeebo in Brazil on 16 April 2010.

platform.heading: A console with mobile roots
platform.text: Zeebo Inc. was formed by Tectoy and Qualcomm. Its console used Qualcomm mobile technology and delivered games through a built-in 3G connection instead of discs. At GDC 2009, the company presented a system intended for households in developing markets.

platform.heading: The intended audience
platform.text: In May 2009, CEO John Rizzo discussed an initial Brazilian rollout, followed by Mexico. The executives described a mix of established games and new titles suited to local audiences. Qualcomm’s Mike Yuen explained their approach to finding that content:

quotes.text: We don't just have to take everything in the Western world and force it on people in another world.
quotes.speaker: Mike Yuen, Qualcomm
quotes.attribution: Interview with Brandon Sheffield, Gamasutra, 20 May 2009

platform.heading: The development environment
platform.text: The May 2009 Developer Guide describes Zeebo software version 1.0 as based on Qualcomm’s BREW 4.0.2 SDK, with OpenGL ES graphics and IHID controller extensions. Its specifications list VGA television output at 640 × 480 in a 4:3 aspect ratio.

platform.heading: Tools and testing
platform.text: The guide covers memory management, controller input, 3D graphics, audio, debugging and game submission. It includes instructions for BREW AppLoader and Logger, loading builds from an SD card, and tuning television output. Developers’ individual accounts describe how they used this environment for particular games.

platform.heading: The surviving collection
platform.text: OpenZeebo’s compilation notes are dated 23 October 2011. They map numeric application IDs to game and system-app names. The archive retains those IDs, the original package variants and the measured file fingerprints, alongside the game histories.
